articles.title: Justin Jefferson scores as many TDs on Sunday as he did in entire 2025 season
articles.summary: It's been a long time since Vikings fans were able to celebrate a score from their All-Pro receiver at home. Sunday's were worth celebrating.
articles.body:
Justin Jefferson had a season to forget in 2025.

Amid quarterback play that ranged from inconsistent to downright bad, the four-time All-Pro wide receiver had the worst season of his career, tallying 84 catches for 1,048 yards and just two touchdowns.

That was with a combination of J.J. McCarthy , Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer throwing him the ball.

On Sunday, Jefferson was back to catching passes from Wentz thanks to a reckless first-quarter hit that left new Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray concussed . But Jefferson and Wentz didn't take long to get on the same page, and Jefferson matched his 2025 touchdown tally on one day against the Green Bay Packers .

With 2:05 remaining in the first half and the Packers holding a 12-3 lead, Jefferson ran a post route, and the Packers jumped offsides. Given a free play, Wentz did the sensible thing and threw the ball deep down the sideline to Jefferson.

Jefferson shed his defender and caught the 39-yard bomb in the back of the end zone for a touchdown.

The touchdown was Jefferson's first since Week 9 of the 2025 season. It was his first at home since Dec. 16, 2024, in a 30-12 win over the Chicago Bears . That season, Jefferson tallied 103 catches for 1,533 yards and 10 touchdowns en route to first team All-Pro honors.

Jefferson added a second touchdown late to cap a wild second-half rally for a 39-22 win . Jefferson finished with 8 catches for 92 yards and 2 touchdowns in addition to a catch for a 2-point conversion.

Both of Jefferson's touchdowns in 2025 were on the road, and he gave Vikings fan a show they hadn't seen in nearly two years with his return to form on Sunday.

It's a welcome sight for Vikings fans, especially considering the loss of Murray to injury in Week 1. It's unclear as of Sunday when Murray will return to football.

Whomever is playing quarterback, the Vikings count on All-Pro level production from Jefferson, who's only 27 years old and remains one of the premier offensive weapons in football.

articles.title: Jaxson Dart Takes Late Hit as Giants, Cowboys Skirmish on Video in NFL Week 1 Rivalry Game
articles.summary: The New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys have both dealt with some down years over the past few seasons, but that doesn't mean their rivalry has cooled off.
articles.body:
The New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys have both dealt with some down years over the past few seasons, but that doesn't mean their rivalry has cooled off.

In the first quarter of the Week 1 matchup between the divisional rivals, Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart ran for a first down before taking a late hit from DeMarvion Overshown. That led to a skirmish between the two sides.

The rivalry between the Cowboys and Giants has always been intense, even in years when the two teams aren't at their best. Last year, their Week 2 matchup went into overtime as Dallas won 40-37. New York responded with a win in their second matchup of the season.

This season, the matchup could be much more important as both teams aim to compete for the playoffs.

Dallas had a tremendous offense last year, but its poor defense kept it from reaching the postseason. The Cowboys made major strides on that end over the offseason and are expected to be a playoff contender, if not a Super Bowl contender.

The Giants perhaps aren't ready to compete for a championship just yet, but it wouldn't be surprising to see them make a run at the playoffs.

Dart had a strong rookie season and should only get better this year, and he has some weapons around him, like Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo. New York also brought in John Harbaugh as its head coach this offseason, and his veteran experience will only help.

Of course, it all starts with Week 1, and the Giants will only be more motivated to get a win after their quarterback took a cheap shot early.

articles.title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo scores in injury return, does a backflip to celebrate in New York's 28-20 victory over Dallas
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo did better on this attempt at a backflip.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo 's leg really is doing fine.

The New York Giants running back suffered a horrific leg injury last season, but he recovered and was back in the lineup for the season opener on Sunday night. And judging by his gymnastic skills, he's feeling quite well.

Skattebo scored the first touchdown of the Sunday night game against the Dallas Cowboys , then got a 10 for the floor exercise portion of the program. He hit a handspring into a backflip and nailed the landing.

He finished with 81 rushing yards on 18 carries. One of those carries, an 8-yard run for a first down, iced the game for the Giants with 1:58 left and the Cowboys out of timeouts.

Skattebo made headlines this offseason when he did a backflip on stage at an event, but he couldn't stick the landing that time. A little more time to heal did him well.

Skattebo already has a reputation as a free spirit. Last season he was a fun story as a rookie for the Giants before a fractured fibula put him on injured reserve. He's back now. There will be plenty of viral moments to follow.

articles.title: NFL to make punishment decision after Jaxson Dart incident in Giants-Cowboys game
articles.summary: The NFL will have a punishment decision to make after an incident involving New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart.
articles.body:
The NFL will have a punishment decision to make after Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown was flagged for a hit on New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart.

Dart scrambled toward the sideline during Sunday night's NFC East matchup before Overshown delivered a hit as the quarterback was going out of bounds. The officials immediately threw a flag for unnecessary roughness, resulting in a 15-yard penalty.

Video of the play shared by Rate the Refs on X shows Overshown making contact with Dart near the sideline. The NFL will now review the play as part of its normal postgame officiating process.

The biggest question will be how the league classifies the hit. It could be considered a late hit because Dart was moving out of bounds when Overshown made contact. However, the league could also determine that Dart was a defenseless player at the time of the hit.

That distinction matters because the two infractions carry different fines under the NFL's 2026 schedule.

A first-offense late hit carries a $11,941 fine, while a first-offense hit on a defenseless player carries a $17,911 fine.

Based on the nature of the play, the more expensive classification could be the one Overshown ultimately receives. However, the NFL has not announced a punishment, so the $17,911 figure remains a projection rather than a confirmed fine.

The league reviews potential violations after games and sends players a letter explaining the infraction and fine if discipline is issued. Players can also appeal the decision.

Overshown will now wait for the league's ruling. The NFL's weekly discipline announcements should provide the answer on whether the Cowboys linebacker receives the $11,941 late-hit fine or the more significant $17,911 penalty for hitting a defenseless player.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Talks Eagles' Desire to Improve After Win vs. Jayden Daniels, Commanders in Week 1
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles started their season with a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders, but Jalen Hurts is far from satisfied with the Week 1 win.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles started their season with a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders, but Jalen Hurts is far from satisfied with the Week 1 win.

After the game, Hurts explained why the Eagles are "hungry to improve."

"We're all also hungry to prove, continue to push forward in the same direction," Hurts said. "And obviously, coach is going to have some things that he wants back. I'm gonna have some throws that I want back. Gonna have some times where, 'Hey, we gotta line up quicker, we need to get down, get set and we gotta come back to the huddle and be urgent.' So, I think for us, and I say it all the time, urgency isn't an option... We're pushing for excellence in everything we do."

Hurts was solid in the season opener as he threw for 203 yards and three touchdowns, but he could have been more efficient as he completed just 14 of his 25 pass attempts.

On defense, the Eagles got to Jayden Daniels just one time for a sack, so they'll be looking to bring more pressure next week.

Philadelphia still has plenty of players on its roster who won a Super Bowl in 2024, and they know that you can't be satisfied with a Week 1 win. Hurts and company will look to continue improving week by week as they march toward the playoffs.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Assesses Bengals' Win vs. Buccaneers, 'Big-Time Players Making Big-Time Plays'
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals started their season with a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as the team looks to make its way back to the playoffs.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals started their season with a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as the team looks to make its way back to the playoffs.

For quarterback Joe Burrow, the win came down to "big-time players making big-time plays."

"It was a great team win. Big-time players making big-time plays in big-time spots," Burrow told reporters (6:25 mark). "I know nobody's satisfied, obviously. It's one week. We still have a lot of football to play, but good stuff."

Burrow used plenty of "big-time players" in the win as he threw to nine different receivers. He went to tight end Mike Gesicki the most, as he collected five receptions for 78 yards and a touchdown.

Burrow finished with 254 yards, a touchdown and an interception on 25-of-35 passing.

"If I didn't have that interception, I'm feeling great walking out of here. You can't make plays like that, so I got to get that fixed," Burrow said. "Offensive line was pretty lights out. I thought we ran the ball, ran the ball well in spots, and you know, I got the got the ball to my guys in space pretty quickly."

Somewhat surprisingly, Ja'Marr Chase had just two receptions for 12 yards, getting four balls from Burrow thrown his way. The good news for the Bengals is that if they were able to get the win without Chase and Burrow connecting, they'll only be more dominant once those two hit their stride.

The Bengals have had a dissapointing three seasons, missing the playoffs in each of the last three years since reaching the AFC Championship game in 2022.

Last year was marred by a bad defense and injuries for Burrow, who played just eight games.

Cincinnati has work to do after Week 1, and Burrow recognized that, but it's fair to say the Bengals can compete for a Super Bowl as long as they stay healthy this year.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh, Justin Herbert Address Chargers' Surprising Loss vs. Cardinals to Open NFL Season
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters his team was "sloppy" and its performance was "uncharacteristic" during a surprising 26-14 loss against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters his team was "sloppy" and its performance was "uncharacteristic" during a surprising 26-14 loss against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

"You get punched. How we respond is what I'm thinking about right now," he added . "There's things to get better at offensively, defensively, and special teams... everyone knows that. Uncharacteristic things happened."

Justin Herbert echoed a theme throughout his postgame comments, meanwhile—a lack of execution:

The Chargers only managed 268 yards on offense, 22 minutes and 29 seconds in time of possession and had two turnovers. Herbert was also sacked three times. From top to bottom, it was rough.

There was a lot of excitement heading into the 2026 season, given the addition of Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator. One game in, the offense is much more of a work in progress than anybody would have anticipated.

articles.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens WR's Status & Fantasy Implications After Week 1
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens will be without one of their wide receivers for a few weeks after an injury in Week 1.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without one of their wide receivers for a few weeks after an injury in Week 1.

Per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, rookie Ja'Kobi Lane suffered a fractured wrist in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts and will undergo further testing and an MRI on Monday.

Lane, who was making his NFL debut on Sunday, came down hard on his left wrist in the end zone while trying to catch a pass from Lamar Jackson in the second quarter. He finished the game with one reception for 11 yards.

Lane was a standout at USC, recording 1,363 yards and 18 touchdowns during his time with the Trojans. The Ravens drafted him in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

Unfortunately for Baltimore, Lane wasn't the only receiver injured against the Colts.

Zay Flowers exited in the second quarter after suffering a hamstring injury and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine his Week 2 status. He was putting together a tremendous game before the injury, collecting 150 yards and a touchdown in less than two quarters.

With Lane set to miss time and Flowers potentially having to miss time as well, fantasy managers might want to look to Rashod Bateman on the waiver wire. Bateman had just one target on Sunday, but that's sure to change in Week 2 if Jackson is without two key receivers.

Tight end Mark Andrews could also see an increase in production in Week 2 after picking up four receptions for 49 yards on Sunday.

The Ravens had a strong start to the Jesse Minter era after picking up the win, but they'll face a New Orleans Saints team that took the Detroit Lions to overtime on Sunday next week.

That should be a manageable game, but it will be tougher if Lane and Flowers aren't on the field.

articles.title: “I’ll never take that for granted”: How Travis Kelce’s hidden $800,000 move changed the story behind his charity controversy
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s charity work came under scrutiny in January after questions emerged over how Eighty-Seven & Running reported its spending. Then cam.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s charity work came under scrutiny in January after questions emerged over how Eighty-Seven & Running reported its spending. Then came a new detail. The foundation had committed $800,000 to communities over the next three years, money that had not yet appeared in its current filings.That disclosure gave a different look at the Kansas City Chiefs tight end’s charitable work. It also came just days after Kelce won the Nationwide Charity Challenge for the third time.How the $800,000 commitment changes the picture around Travis Kelce’s foundationA January 2026 report from The Arizona Republic raised questions about Eighty-Seven & Running’s finances, saying federal filings from 2021 through 2024 showed only 41 cents of every dollar going toward charitable work.A source close to Travis Kelce later told People that the filings did not show the complete picture. The source said the foundation had committed $800,000 over the next three years, with those funds set to appear in future filings once they are deployed.The same source said that counting the committed money would put the foundation at more than 80% directed toward charitable causes.Travis Kelce’s business manager Aaron Eanes also addressed the reporting. He said some costs had been “mistakenly reported under management rather than allocated adequately to program services.” Eanes added that management fees fell significantly in 2024 and reached zero in 2025.That explanation came as CharityWatch questioned the foundation’s structure. Laurie Styron, the organization’s executive director, told The Arizona Republic, “That’s not how charities work.”Still, Travis Kelce’s recent charitable record gives more context. He founded Eighty-Seven & Running in 2015, with the foundation focused on helping disadvantaged youth.Travis Kelce’s Kansas City work goes beyond the foundation’s filingsKelce has also built a long-running relationship with Operation Breakthrough. The Chiefs said on Dec 4, 2025, that his work with the organization and its Ignition Lab had helped more than 1,000 Kansas City high school students since the lab opened.That same day, Kelce spoke about being named the Chiefs’ Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee. Reflecting on his connection to Kansas City and Cleveland Heights, he said, “Being able to give back to Kansas City and to my hometown, places that have done so much for me, has been a dream come true, and I’ll never take that for granted.” He made the comment in his statement after the Chiefs announced his 2025 nomination.Then, on January 7, 2026, Kelce learned on the New Heights podcast that he had won the Nationwide Charity Challenge. The victory added another $35,000 donation to his charity of choice, Operation Breakthrough.So, while questions around Eighty-Seven & Running remain part of the conversation, the newly disclosed $800,000 commitment adds an important piece to the financial picture.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los Eagles doblegan a los Commanders y los Vikings sorprenden a los Packers
articles.summary: Primera semana de la NFL
articles.body: Los Philadelphia Eagles lograron un trabajado triunfo por 24-22 en la primera semana de la NFL contra los Washington Commanders, mientras que los Minnesota Vikings dieron la sorpresa con una paliza a los Green Bay Packers (39-22), con un parcial de 22-0 en el último período. Los Eagles comenzaron su temporada con victoria, pero tuvieron que sufrir hasta el final ante los Commanders. Fue la defensa de Philadelphia la que evitó una conversión de dos puntos en los últimos segundos que igualaría el duelo para la franquicia capitalina. En una noche poco brillante por tierra, el mariscal de campo Jalen Hurts lanzó para 203 yardas, con tres pases de anotación. En los Commanders, Jayden Daniels sumó 164 yardas con dos pases de 'touchdown'. En Minneapolis, los Vikings se sobrepusieron al amargo debut del 'quarterback' Kyler Murray, quien se retiró por un trauma en la cabeza en el primer período tras un choque con el 'safety' de los Packers Javon Bullard. Le reemplazó Carson Wentz y lo hizo de la mejor forma, con tres pases de anotación y un total de 130 yardas lanzadas. Los Vikings cerraron el partido con 29 puntos consecutivos entre el final del tercer período y el último cuarto. Tendrá que esperar su debut del estadounidense de origen cubano Fernando Mendoza, elegido con el número uno absoluto en el último draft por Las Vegas Raiders. Con Kirk Cousins de titular (160 yardas lanzadas, 3 pases de anotación y 2 interceptaciones), los Raiders ganaron 27-13 a los Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson Reacts to 2 TDs in Vikings' Win vs. Packers After 2025 NFL Season Scoring Stats
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson only had two touchdowns all of last season, a major disappointment for one of the elite wideouts in football.
articles.body:
Justin Jefferson only had two touchdowns all of last season, a major disappointment for one of the elite wideouts in football.

He matched that total on Sunday, however, reeling in eight passes for 92 yards and two scores during a 39-22 comeback win against the Green Bay Packers.

"I guess you could say it was a get-back from last year," Jefferson said during an appearance on SportsCenter . "Really a grind in the offseason, just putting in that work and expecting a lot from myself, to come in here and continue to show that I'm the best receiver in the league. So to come out here and help my team win, getting two touchdowns, that was big for us."

Both were thrown by Carson Wentz, who was thrust into relief duty after starter Kyler Murray left the game in the first half with a concussion.

Wentz didn't have many reps over the summer, with Murray and JJ McCarthy competing for the starting position, but he was named the backup nonetheless and threw for 133 yards and three scores on Sunday.

"It was a different process [this summer], I'm not going to lie," he told reporters after the win. "But I've stayed as ready as I could. Mental reps, reps after practice, whatever that looks like, and at the end of the day leaving it in god's hands. I'm confident in what I bring to the table, what I can do and if my number gets called and that I can step up when needed. So who knew how it was going to play out? None of us did in here, but I trusted god through it. Football is a funny game."

He trusted Jefferson too, and it was a winning bet.

articles.title: Ben Johnson Doubles Down on Wanting Historic NFL Offense After Bears' Win vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson said in August that he wants to be the NFL's highest-scoring offense ever, and after Week 1, he's off to a good start.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson said in August that he wants to be the NFL's highest-scoring offense ever, and after Week 1, he's off to a good start.

The Bears beat the Carolina Panthers 59-37 on Sunday, and Johnson doubled down on his comments afterwards.

"That will always be the goal," he told reporters . "We want to be the highest scoring, we want to have the most wins, we want to win Super Bowls. That's what we do. We didn't get into this profession trying to be mediocre or average."

The highest-scoring offense in NFL history was the 2013 Denver Broncos, who averaged 37.9 points per game behind a record-breaking season from legendary quarterback Peyton Manning.

The Bears might not have Manning under center, but they have a promising young quarterback in Caleb Williams, who threw for 269 yards and a pair of touchdowns.

What was more impressive was the Bears' run game, which accounted for 291 yards of the team's 552 yards. D'Andre Swift had 124 yards and three touchdowns, while Kyle Monangai added 100 yards and a score. Williams picked up 65 yards and two scores on the ground.

It's hard to imagine Chicago will be able to match its offense in Week 2, but Johnson made it clear that he has every intention to continue piling on points. The Bears will look for another offensive showing against the Minnesota Vikings next week.

articles.title: Cowboys Defense Called Out By NFL Fans After Loss vs. Jaxson Dart, Malik Nabers, Giants in Week 1
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys spent their offseason upgrading their defense, but those supposed upgrades were nowhere to be found on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys spent their offseason upgrading their defense, but those supposed upgrades were nowhere to be found on Sunday.

The Cowboys dropped their season opener to the New York Giants, 28-20.

After the poor showing in the loss, fans called out Dallas' defense.

The Cowboys had one of the worst defenses in the NFL last year, giving up the most points per game (30.1) and the third-most yards per game (377.0). That negated a tremendous season from the offense, which was near the top of the league in most statistical categories.

The thing separating Dallas from having an elite team was its poor defense, so the Cowboys made Christian Parker their defensive coordinator and added players like Caleb Downs, Quinnen Williams and more.

It's only one game, but it's likely hard for Cowboys fans not to be discouraged by what they saw against the Giants.

To be fair, the offense wasn't doing much either, as Dak Prescott had just 175 yards, two touchdowns and a pair of interceptions on 22-of-34 passing, but the Giants also dominated time of possession.

If Dallas' defense can't stop a rebuilding group like the New York Giants, it's hard to imagine it will have success against teams like the Baltimore Ravens, Philadelphia Eagles, San Francisco 49ers and others it will face this season.

articles.title: Giants’ offense rolls over the Cowboys to give coach John Harbaugh a 28-20 win in his debut
articles.summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Jaxson Dart connected with Isaiah Likely for two touchdowns and Devin Singletary on another, Cam Skattebo ran for one in his first game back from injury, and the New York Giants opened the season by beating the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on Sunday night in John Harbaugh’s debut as coach.
articles.body: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Jaxson Dart connected with Isaiah Likely for two touchdowns and Devin Singletary on another, Cam Skattebo ran for one in his first game back from injury, and the New York Giants opened the season by beating the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on Sunday night in John Harbaugh’s debut as coach. Dart made one smart throw after another, mixing in a series of well-timed runs to keep the defense off balance. He finished 23 of 29 for 230 yards passing, plus 54 rushing, including a couple of slides and a dive to avoid the unnecessary hits that punctuated his rookie year. Likely made eight catches on eight targets for 78 yards in his New York debut after following Harbaugh from Baltimore, extending the training camp trend when he was consistently Dart’s top option. No. 1 receiver Malik Nabers, playing for the first time since going down with a torn ACL in his right knee 350 days ago, had six catches for 69 yards. Back on the field more than 10 months since breaking his right fibula and dislocating his right ankle in gruesome fashion, Skattebo rumbled for 81 yards on 18 carries. After getting in hot water for doing a backflip earlier this summer, Skattebo brought back his signature celebration after running into the end zone untouched for the Giants’ first points of the season. Dak Prescott threw a costly interception just before halftime but otherwise played well for Dallas, completing 22 of 34 passes for 175 yards and TD tosses to CeeDee Lamb and Javonte Williams, who also ran for a touchdown. Dallas benefited from a series of defensive pass interference calls that extended drives. The Cowboys hurt themselves with penalties — eight of them for 85 yards, not counting an early intentional delay of game. That included a taunting call on Williams after he scored that contributed to Brandon Aubrey missing the ensuing extra point from farther out and a facemask flag on Donovan Ezeiruaku just before the two-minute warning. Their defense also did not look as improved on defense as they had hoped, at least in Week 1. After allowing the most points in the NFL last season at 30.1 a game, this was not far off, despite a new coordinator and some additional talent.

articles.title: Chargers Fall Flat After Jim Harbaugh’s Bold Justin Herbert Prediction
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers appeared to be an easy pick to win in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Justin Herbert and his team were taking on an Arizona Cardinals...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers appeared to be an easy pick to win in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Justin Herbert and his team were taking on an Arizona Cardinals squad led by Jacoby Brissett , picked by many experts to be chasing a top pick in next year's draft.

That is why the games are played, as the Cardinals dominated en route to a 26-14 victory. Chargers fans were left in shock after an offseason full of hype. Mike McDaniel showed up as the new offensive coordinator and was supposed to fix the unit's woes. 14 total points was not what anyone outside of Arizona had in mind.

This shocking loss also came after head coach John Harbaugh offered Herbert the ultimate praise.

Justin Herbert Falls Flat Amid Massive Hype

Harbaugh recently took part in an interview with NFL legend Michael Irvin via Netflix Sports. The head coach declared Herbert would go down as the "best ever" quarterback once his career is at an end. Sunday made it seem like the critics of Herbert have been right.

It is fair to note this was Week 1 and the season opener has become a rough watch for many teams as the preseason features fewer starters every passing year. Yet 14 points at home against the Cardinals is a rough outing no matter what week it says on the schedule.

One analyst, Yahoo Sports' Matt Harmon, predicted the Chargers would score "50-plus" in Week 1 with the new duo of Herbert and McDaniel. So it was not just Harbaugh hyping up his squad. The Chargers were expected to win this game and win it big.

A fun way to watch every NFL season is to take part in a "survivor pool." This means picking one team to win per week, and not being able to choose the same team twice. The Chargers were a top pick in Week 1 and as betting analyst Ben Fawkes notes , over 30% of those in the Circa Sports Survivor pool were eliminated thanks to the Chargers.

That is a brutal way to begin a season and shows how big of an upset this game was in the NFL world. Those who went with the Chargers may now be rooting against the team the remainder of the season.

This was a brutal loss for Los Angeles in general and because of the upcoming schedule. The team has a bye in Week 7, but faces the Las Vegas Raiders , Buffalo Bills , Seattle Seahawks , Denver Broncos , and Kansas City Chiefs before the bye. The Raiders picked up a win in Week 1 and the next four teams are all legitimate Super Bowl contenders. That makes the loss to the Cardinals even more frustrating.

The Chargers scored three points in last season's playoff exit and managed 14 in Week 1 this season. Herbert and the offense can only go up from here.

articles.title: DK Metcalf's Updated Fantasy Outlook as Aaron Rodgers Hypes WR After Steelers' Win vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf didn't seem to be on the same page during the Pittsburgh Steelers' 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, as the veteran wideout was targeted 10 times but only finished with four receptions for 40 yards.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf didn't seem to be on the same page during the Pittsburgh Steelers' 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, as the veteran wideout was targeted 10 times but only finished with four receptions for 40 yards.

While the production ultimately was disappointing, expect the high target share to continue.

"Love my guys, love DK," Rodgers told reporters (5:05 mark) after the win. "You know he's had such a great camp, I'm gonna keep going to him. Give him as many opportunities as possible."

Metcalf easily finished with the most targets on the team and was well ahead of Michael Pittman Jr. (three targets) in that regard, though Pittman turned his look into three receptions for 58 yards.

From a fantasy perspective, that usage is a good sign. From an overall production standpoint, however, it's a concerning trend. Last season Metcalf also led the team in targets (99) but his 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns across 15 games wasn't elite production. His 12.9 fantasy points per game in PPR leagues was tied for 20th in the NFL, making him more of a flex consideration.

Thus far in 2026, it seems like he's trending in that direction again, though we're obviously just one week in. If you drafted him to be a WR2, maybe temper those expectations.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love admits he’d do one thing differently on the failed Vikings sneak
articles.summary: Jordan Love threw for 387 yards on Sunday. He ran a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter and gained nothing. The Green Bay Packers led 22-...
articles.body:
Jordan Love threw for 387 yards on Sunday. He ran a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter and gained nothing.

The Green Bay Packers led 22-10 in the third quarter and lost 39-22 at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Minnesota scored 22 points in the fourth quarter. Green Bay scored none.

Jordan Love says he would have gone with the other play call

"Yeah, I ran a QB sneak," Love said. "You know, they did a good job stopping it. You know, I think there's some stuff I could have done better with my operation and even, you know, with the play call. You know, we had two plays called right there. Went with the quarterback sneak. Thought we could get it, and we didn't."

He walked through the mechanics when asked what he could have done differently on a play with so few moving parts.

"I think QB sneaks, whenever you've got the gaps filled, trying to find those open gaps," Love said. "Maybe let the rush come and try to find one of those open gaps and dive forward instead of maybe just going right up the middle. So there are some things you can do differently right there. We'll look at it."

"And then I think, like I said, we had two plays called right there," he said. "And obviously the QB sneak didn't work. Hindsight, wish I would have went with the other play."

Love said he checked to the sneak because he believed in it. "Just thought we can get it," he said. "We've ran a lot of QB sneaks in the past. I felt confident that we'd be able to get it."

The 387 yards came with four sacks and a fumble

Love finished 21-of-42 and was sacked four times for 34 yards. One of the sacks came loose and Minnesota recovered it, and LaFleur described that one as a protection bust rather than a quarterback error.

"I know one of them was a protection breakdown," the head coach said. "We called a certain jet. I don't think he adjusted the protection. We slid one way. We had nobody for the guy in the B-gap. So that's a bust."

Aaron Banks did not play. "I think he's made progress, but he wasn't ready yet," LaFleur said of the left guard.

Green Bay was also without Micah Parsons , who is on the reserve/physically unable to perform list, and Josh Jacobs, who is on the Commissioner's Exempt List .

"You're playing this defense, you know it's going to be pressure," Love said. "You know that's part of it. So, like I said, you know, we'll look back at the film, but there's a lot of just missed opportunities, which I wish, a couple of plays I wish we could get back."

Green Bay scored on its first drive of the game and did not score after the third quarter. Minnesota put up 22 in the fourth, three touchdowns inside a span of 2 minutes and 39 seconds.

"I definitely think you look at that fourth quarter, they got the momentum and they started rolling," Love said. "And that's where we kind of fell apart. And, you know, I think obviously being in this away environment, the noise, everything, everybody, the communication has got to be 100%."

He rejected the idea that Minnesota did anything new to cause it.

"It's not like they changed the looks a crazy amount," Love said. "They're running the same stuff. So we just got to find ways to execute."

A reporter asked whether the postgame language starts to ring hollow when it matches what he said after losses last season.

"No, it just comes down, honestly, it just comes down to there's a couple plays here and there in the game that we've got to go out there and make," Love said. "If we do that, it's a different game. Unfortunately, we didn't do that today. The message is still the message. We'll get back to work, continue to keep working. That's all we can do."

Green Bay is at the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.

articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett and the Arizona Cardinals are riding high after an exceptional performance on Sunday afternoon. Arizona is coming off of a 26-14 victory over...
articles.body:
and the Arizona Cardinals are riding high after an exceptional performance on Sunday afternoon.

Arizona is coming off of a 26-14 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers . The game flow ensured a relatively close battle, but the Cardinals pulled away late to earn a signature win.

Brissett spoke to media following the game, including praising two teammates that put together strong performances on Sunday. Read more on Brissett's interaction with media below.

Brissett Strongly Praises Supporting Cast

While the 33-year-old Brissett is coming off os a stout performance, his teammates did much of the lifting in compliment. Arizona's quarterback acknowledged as much following the game ( Arizona Cardinals X ).

A particular subject of praise was wide receiver Kendrick Bourne . The 10-year NFL vet came in at second on the team in receptions (8) and yards (75) on Sunday. This led to praise in no uncertain terms from Brissett.

"I'm pretty sure none of y'all had him on your fantasy. He was just in the right spot at the right time on a lot of plays. We put him there because we trust him there."

Bourne has built a successful NFL career over nine seasons, but is firmly Arizona's third wide receiver in 2026. Expectations heading into week one were relatively tempered, as Trey McBride , Michael Wilson , and Marvin Harrison Jr. are generally going to be prioritized.

That wasn't the case today. Not only did Bourne make key receptions, he is also playing a major role as a perimeter blocker.

Beyond Bourne is rookie running back Jeremiyah Love . The Notre Dame product is now one game into his NFL career after pushing through an ankle injury to play in his debut. The third overall pick in April even scored Arizona's first touchdown of 2026.

Brissett again left no stones unturned with his praise of the 21-year-old.

While Love's workload wasn't exceptionally large volume wise, he did make a difference. Love only mustered two receptions, but is continuing to show that he is a threat in the passing game nonetheless. The dynamic with Tyler Allgeier is also setting up to be mutually beneficial for each as the season progresses.

What Win Means for Cardinals Moving Forward

Week one overreactions run abundant in each NFL season.

While the Cardinals are showing encouraging signs at the moment, the team faces a gauntlet schedule moving forward. This includes the Seattle Seahawks and San Fransisco 49ers in back-to-back weeks, as well as the Los Angeles Rams in a week six duel.

Mike LaFleur is a sharp play-caller to this point. Arizona's offense is more bold than expected. The defense is heading into week two with a major victory to take with them.

There are personnel reasons that have potential to slow down the momentum as well, including Brissett's potential limitations. Until then, Arizona will celebrate starting the LaFleur era on a high note.

The Cardinals and Brissett returns to action next Sunday against Seattle.

articles.title: Malik Nabers Reveals Deciding Factor in Playing Giants' Week 1 Win vs. Cowboys After Injury Rehab
articles.summary: Malik Nabers was on the fence about playing in the New York Giants' season opener against the Dallas Cowboys as he continued his rehab from a torn ACL, but the wide receiver ultimately decided to suit up.
articles.body:
Malik Nabers was on the fence about playing in the New York Giants' season opener against the Dallas Cowboys as he continued his rehab from a torn ACL, but the wide receiver ultimately decided to suit up.

For Nabers, the decision to play was made not long before kickoff. He even told his family not to come to the game incase he decided not play.

"The deciding factor was just when I got out there, I just felt good. I got a little chill through my body," Nabers said. "And I was like, 'Yeah, it's time.'"

Nabers added that going through his warmups made him feel confident enough to play.

"I felt really good. Running around, I was catching really good, stretched really good, warmed up pretty well," he said. "I just felt like it was time to go."

Nabers put together a solid outing in his first game since last September, hauling in six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 win over the Giants' divisional rival.

Nabers had a tremendous rookie season in 2024 when he recorded 1,204 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, but a torn ACL in late September last year meant that he missed most of his second season.

Now, Nabers is back and looking to pick up where he left off. Taking down the Cowboys was certainly a good start.

articles.title: Packers extend sickening losing streak to 6 games
articles.summary: The Packers haven't won a real football game since Dec. 7 of last year. Sunday's collapse extended the losing streak to six sickening games.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers haven't won a real football game since Dec. 7 of last year. Sunday's collapse in Minneapolis, featuring 29 unanswered points and a historic win for the Minnesota Vikings , extended the team's losing streak to six games, including the playoffs. According to Rob Demovsky of ESPN , this represents the Packers' longest losing streak since the 1990-1991 seasons, or pre-Brett Favre.

And this isn't your average six-game losing streak. No, fans of the Packers have been put through a gauntlet of misery since last December. It's one thing to be talent-starved and struggling to compete week in and week out. Season-wrecking injuries and historic collapses from good teams with real expectations have made this one of the most sickening losing streaks in the franchise's long history.

On Dec. 7, 2025, Keisean Nixon 's leaping interception of Caleb Williams in the end zone with 22 seconds to go improved the Packers' record to 9-3-1.

Since then, the Packers have suffered the following defeats, in order:

Week 15: The Packers led the AFC-leading Denver Broncos 23-14 in the third quarter. Season-ending injuries to Zach Tom (now Zach Bako-Bewele) and Micah Parsons begin a spiral, and the Packers end up losing 34-26 when the Broncos score 20 of the game's final 23 points.

Week 16: The Packers lost Jordan Love to a concussion but led the Bears 6-0 at half, 13-3 after three quarters and 16-6 deep into the fourth quarter at Soldier Field. However, Romeo Doubs failed to recover an onside kick with 1:59 to go, Caleb Williams threw a game-tying touchdown pass on fourth down with 24 seconds to go, Malik Willis was stopped on fourth down in Bears territory to open overtime and Williams threw a walk-off 46-yard touchdown pass to win the game in overtime.

Week 17: In a game without Jordan Love and Lamar Jackson because of injury, future Hall of Famer Derrick Henry takes over, rushing for 216 yards and four touchdowns in a memorable primetime performance at Lambeau Field, and the Packers give up 307 total rushing yards in a 41-24 loss that clinched the NFC North title for the Bears . Green Bay becomes the first team ever to lose back-to-back games while not punting in either game.

Week 18: With nothing on the line in terms of playoff seeding, the Packers rest most veterans and start Clayton Tune at quarterback against Brian Flores in the season finale. What unfolds is one of the worst single-game passing performances in Packers history. Green Bay is shut out until the final moments and loses the game, 16-3. Tune completes six passes for 34 yards, takes four sacks for -41 yards and finishes with -7 net passing yards.

NFC Wild Card Round: The Packers raced out to a 21-3 lead at halftime in Chicago , but the Bears scored 13 straight points to open the second half and then stunned the Packers with back-to-back touchdowns to finish off the comeback, including Caleb Williams' go-ahead touchdown pass to D.J. Moore with 1:43 left. Brandon McManus missed two field goals and an extra point in the 31-27 loss. The Bears outscored the Packers 25-6 in the fourth quarter. The Packers held leads of 21-6 and 27-16 in the fourth quarter but were still eliminated.

Week 1: The Packers took a 22-10 lead deep into the third quarter of the season opener, but the Vikings ripped off 29 straight points to win 39-22 and become the first NFL team to trail by at least 12 points with under 20 minutes to go and win by at least 17 points. Green Bay is outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter.

Will the losing streak finally end next Sunday? The Packers are headed to New York to play the Jets , who soundly beat the Tennessee Titans 23-10 in the season opener. There's no room to look too far ahead. Come next Sunday, the Packers will be roughly 9.5 months removed from their last real victory. Matt LaFleur's team just needs to get back in the win column and start erasing the awful taste of this losing streak at MetLife Stadium.

articles.title: NFL results: Chicago Bears, Buffalo Bills & Baltimore Ravens win on record-breaking Sunday
articles.summary: After kicking off the NFL season with a Super Bowl rematch and a trip to Australia, week one continued with a record-breaking Sunday.
articles.body:
After kicking off the season with a Super Bowl rematch and a trip to Australia, week one continued with a record-breaking Sunday.

The Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens showed why they are favourites to win the AFC Conference, and the Chicago Bears made a statement as they racked up 59 points.

Those wins contributed to an NFL record for the most points scored on the opening Sunday of the season since the league merger in 1970.

Here's what you need to know from the opening weekend.

The Bills changed their head coach in a bid to finally reach the Super Bowl with star quarterback Josh Allen, promoting offensive co-ordinator Joe Brady to the top job.

His first game was a big test, coming against last season's meanest defence, and the lead changed hands eight times in a thriller at the Houston Texans.

Running back David Montgomery scored three touchdowns on his Houston debut, but Allen ran in two touchdowns and passed for two more.

The 2024 season's Most Valuable Player was almost intercepted as he launched a hopeful pass into the endzone with less than two minutes remaining.

But on the next play 30-year-old Allen held his nerve with a 34-yard throw to Joshua Palmer that clinched a 36-31 win.

Buffalo's first five games are against potential Super Bowl contenders, so they needed to hit the ground running.

After missing last season's play-offs the Baltimore Ravens brought an end to John Harbaugh's 18-year tenure as head coach, and they made a flying start under successor Jesse Minter.

Zay Flowers, who became the NFL's fourth highest-paid wide receiver in the off-season, made five catches for a career-high 150 yards and a touchdown in the first half alone at the Indianapolis Colts.

Derrick Henry also scored twice before half-time to move into third on the all-time list for rushing touchdowns, then added another as the Ravens cruised to a 41-23 win.

But there was concern for Baltimore as Flowers and rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane missed the second half with hamstring and wrist injuries respectively.

The Ravens' impressive win was soon eclipsed by the Chicago Bears, who were level with the Carolina Panthers at 31-31 midway through the third quarter before romping to victory.

Running back D'Andre Swift finished with three touchdowns in a 59-37 road win - the highest-scoring week one game in NFL history and Chicago's highest score since 1980.

After leading the Bears to their first division title in seven years last season, head coach Ben Johnson has set some lofty targets.

"We want to be the highest scoring. We want to have the most wins. We want to win Super Bowls," he said.

Harbaugh is now in charge of a promising young roster at the New York Giants, and his first game came on a poignant night at the MetLife Stadium, which hosted the football World Cup final in July.

Two days after the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the Giants honoured New York's first responders and those impacted by the attacks with a series of tributes before Sunday's primetime game.

The Giants then produced a convincing 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys, with second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart passing for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while fit-again running back Cam Skattebo rushed for another.

It was a balanced team performance with a disciplined defence, a trademark of Harbaugh's team throughout his time in Baltimore.

With the New York Knicks ending their long wait for an NBA championship this year, there is genuine belief that the Giants can also get back in play-off contention.

The Arizona Cardinals have been tipped by many to finish with the NFL's worst record, while the Los Angeles Chargers are seen as play-off contenders.

But the Chargers were humbled on their own turf at SoFi Stadium, which will host Super Bowl 61 in February.

The Cardinals are trying to make a fresh start having brought in Mike LaFleur as head coach and released quarterback Kyler Murray, and they dominated possession in a 26-14 win.

Murray, who went on to earn the starting role with the Minnesota Vikings, made a wretched start at home to the Green Bay Packers, coached by LaFleur's older brother Matt.

Murray's first pass with the Vikings was intercepted, and the former first overall draft pick then suffered a concussion before being replaced by veteran Carson Wentz.

Despite falling 22-10 down late in the third quarter, the Vikings fought back to win 39-22, with Justin Jefferson claiming two well-taken touchdowns and a two-point conversion.

The Vikings have had nine starting quarterbacks since Jefferson was named offensive player of the year for 2022, and the wide receiver looked back to his best.

Although the Cincinnati Bengals have one of the NFL's most potent offences, they have been let down by their defence in the past three seasons.

The front office tried to remedy that in the off-season, and the revamped defence was impressive in their opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Three of last season's 11 defeats came despite scoring at least 34 points, and again the Bengals had little trouble scoring against the Bucs.

This time their defence did their job too, though, recording four sacks and forcing four fumbles. All four were recovered by Cincinnati, with one returned for a defensive touchdown in a 33-27 home win.

If the Bengals can maintain that consistency - and quarterback Joe Burrow avoids another injury-hit season - they could have realistic hope of returning to the Super Bowl, having played the last time the big game was held in LA in 2022.

articles.title: New season, same Cowboys. Dallas once again smashes its fans' hopes in New York face-plant
articles.summary: Where do you even start after this flop of a performance? There's so much blame to go around, everybody gets a third serving. The defense will come in for th...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me 30 times, call me a Dallas Cowboys fan.

Once again, the Cowboys and their defenders rolled into a season insisting that this was The Year, that Dak Prescott was in his prime, that the newly retooled defense would complement an explosive offense, that the highest of hopes were now in play.

It all sure seemed like awfully big talk for a team that finished 7-9-1 last season. But Prescott sported a Super Bowl XXX shirt — the last time Dallas won the game — during training camp this summer, and team owner Jerry Jones left no doubt about his expectations.

"Contend for a Super Bowl," Jones said earlier this summer . "Those are the kinds of things that I don't believe are … outlandish or a reach to expect."

Yeah, about that. After Sunday night's season debut, a 28-20 pantsing at the hands of the division rival New York Giants , perhaps Dallas ought to set some more realistic goals. Like, oh, not allowing touchdowns on three straight possessions? Or not getting bamboozled by the exact same play four times in less than two minutes? Maybe start there and worry about the stretch goals later.

"As a football team, we were pretty poor," head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the game. "Just give Coach [John] Harbaugh and his team a bunch of credit. They were the more physical team tonight. That's certainly not our standard … This is a humbling business, and we got humbled."

Where do you even start after this flop of a performance? There's so much blame to go around, everybody gets a third serving. The defense will come in for the most severe scorching, and deservedly so.

New defensive coordinator Christian Parker's men looked overmatched and underprepared, surrendering both lightning-quick and slow-bleed drives on the night. Most damning of all, the Cowboys let the Giants run the same play — Jaxson Dart finding running back Devin Singletary wide open in the left flat — time after time in the fourth quarter with the game still reachable at 21-14. Singletary finally found the end zone, capping off a second straight eight-plus-minute second-half drive.

"He'll learn from it, we'll learn from it," Schottenheimer said of Parker. "He's gonna be hardest on himself anyways, he and the defensive staff. But at the end of the day, when you look at the numbers, I mean, they were 4-of-4 in the red zone. They were 9-of-11 with a kneel down on third down. It's just not good enough. And so we gotta figure out why, and we gotta do it in a hurry."

Prescott and the offense had their own struggles, particularly in the first half. The killer: an interception that Prescott unwisely underthrew while trying to get the ball out of bounds. The Giants flew 55 yards down the field in 29 seconds, scoring just before the half, and then methodically stomped down the field in 8:01 to open the third, turning a 7-7 tie into a 21-7 lead without Dallas ever touching the ball.

"That's unfortunately what we call a double dip," Schottenheimer said, "and they double-dipped us."

Prescott led Dallas into the end zone every time he touched the ball in the second half. Unfortunately, the Cowboys had only two possessions during the entire second half, with New York controlling the ball — and squeezing the life out of Dallas — for nearly 22 of 30 minutes. You can't make plays when you're on the sideline. And Prescott ended the game with a paltry 175 yards on 22-of-34 passing, with two touchdowns and that one backbreaker of an interception.

"It's one game. This is a long year," Prescott insisted. "We've got to make sure we use it as a lesson: stick together. One of two things can happen. We can get better from it, or we can allow it to derail us. And I know what I'm gonna do."

Unlike many markets, where bandwagon Dallas fans outnumber the local ones whenever the Cowboys come to town, the Giants' Big Blue nation swarmed the Dallas infidels. Even outnumbered, Cowboys fans had no problem talking tough on the walk in to MetLife Stadium, but the way out was surely much quieter from the Dallas contingent.

"We lost mile 1 of a 17-mile marathon, and we have to be better," Schottenheimer said. "We will be better. The only way to do that is to get back to work."

Next up for the Cowboys: another divisional matchup, at home against Washington. It's a long season, and it still could very well end with Dallas hoisting a Lombardi Trophy at the end of it. But organizational collapses like this make it very tough to believe that's anywhere close.

"It sucks to lose. It damn sure sucks to lose the first one to this team in a division game, but [we're] still optimistic," Prescott said. "That doesn't change our goals, doesn't change how we feel about our team."

It probably won't change the way Cowboys fans feel about their team, either. But you do have to wonder how many more underachievements like this have to happen before those fans start asking some really hard questions, both of their team and themselves.
