articles.title: 10 Most Memorable Injury Comebacks in Recent Sports History
articles.summary: In December, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL, ending his 2025 season and putting his immediate playing future in doubt. Nine months later, Mahomes is set to return to face the Denver Broncos in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
In December, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL, ending his 2025 season and putting his immediate playing future in doubt. Nine months later, Mahomes is set to return to face the Denver Broncos in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.

While Mahomes' return in such a short time is one of the bigger storylines of Week 1, it could still be a minor footnote in his Hall of Fame career. Of course, it could also become one of the more memorable injury returns in recent memory.

If Mahomes is close to 100 percent this season and puts Kansas City back in the Super Bowl mix, his reemergence against a divisional foe will be difficult to forget.

Could a triumphant Mahomes recovery find a place in the pantheon of recent sports injury returns? That remains to be seen. But if so, he'll have plenty of company.

Here, we've examined the 10 most memorable injury returns from the past 25 years.

Adrian Peterson Returns from Torn ACL to Become NFL MVP

With Mahomes' return looming, it's probably appropriate that we begin our list here. Adrian Peterson's 2012 return from a torn ACL and MCL remains the NFL's gold standard for coming back from severe knee injuries.

The Minnesota Vikings star running back suffered the injury on December 24, 2011. It was the sort of injury that would have ended a running back's career in an earlier era.

Less than nine months later, though, Peterson was back on the field to face the Jacksonville Jaguars in Minnesota's opener. He rushed for 84 yards and two touchdowns while helping the Vikings achieve an overtime victory.

In the ensuing weeks, Peterson proved that he wasn't just back. He was as good as ever.

"Each week, I feel myself getting better and just try to stay on path," Peterson said during the season, per ESPN's Kevin Seifert .

Peterson went on to rush for a career-best 2,097 yards while starting all 16 games and was named the NFL's Most Valuable Player for his efforts. To this day, he remains the last non-quarterback to be named the NFL MVP.

Some returns are memorable because they involved a single staggering injury. In the case of Tiger Woods' return to the pinnacle of golf, it was about a return to form that had seemed lost to time.

Once considered the most feared competitor in the sport, Woods spent years away from contention while battling persistent back issues, multiple surgeries and a 2017 spinal-fusion procedure.

During that time, it felt like fans might never see Woods win another major tournament. His last PGA win had come in 2013, and by 2017, he had fallen to No. 1,199 in the World Golf Rankings (h/t BBC.com ).

However, Woods' dedication to his sport and his desire to achieve greatness led to one of the most memorable moments in recent sporting history—a victory at the 2019 Masters.

Woods' return to form had actually come the previous year, when he earned his 80th PGA win at the PGA Tour Championship. However, his win at Augusta remains the more iconic comeback victory because of the tournament's profile, the level of competition and Woods' long layoff. It was his first major win since 2008.

Alex Smith Returns From a Life-Threatening Leg Injury

Alex Smith had many milestones during his 16-year NFL career, but he may be best remembered for his return from a horrific 2018 leg injury.

During a game against the Houston Texans on Nov. 18, 2018, the Washington Commanders quarterback sustained a compound spiral fracture of his right tibia and fibula. While the initial injury itself was bad enough, the complications that followed nearly took Smith's life .

Following his initial surgery, Smith developed a life-threatening flesh-eating bacterial infection. Saving Smith's leg—and his life—required extensive tissue removal, reconstruction using muscle from his quad, and 17 total surgeries.

Unsurprisingly, the entire ordeal left a lasting impact on Smith's physical ability.

"I cannot play or do anything without wearing a brace or some kind of device," Smith said, per Lindsay Berra of Men's Health . "Because I have drop foot, I need it to give me a little bounce."

While many in Smith's position would consider themselves fortunate just to walk, he was determined to play football again. In 2020, he did just that.

Smith made his return to action in a Week 5 game against the Los Angeles Rams in relief of starter Kyle Allen. He made his first start since the injury in Week 10 and went on to make six starts for Washington, going 5-1 and helping deliver an NFC East title.

While Smith retired after the 2020 season, he only did so after engineering what was unquestionably the greatest comeback of his career.

New team takes top spot in latest CFB AP poll

Bethany Hamilton Survives Shark Attack to Become National Champion

In 2003, Bethany Hamilton was a 13-year-old rising surfing star. In October of that year, she was attacked by a tiger shark off the coast of Kauai, Hawaii, and lost her left arm in the attack.

Despite the terrifying incident and critical injury, Hamilton was back in the water within weeks. She adapted her paddling and pop-up techniques and used a custom board to return to competition.

Just 10 weeks later, Hamilton took fifth place in her age group at a National Scholastic Surfing Association (NSSA) meet. She also won the 2004 ESPY for Best Comeback Athlete.

"It was definitely a good start," Hamilton said, per NBC News .

In 2005, roughly a year-and-a-half after the attack, Hamilton took first place in the NSSA National Championship under-18 division.

"[People] can do whatever they want if they just set their heart to it, and just never give up, and just go out there and do it," Hamilton said in a 2005 interview with CNN .

Hamilton went on to have a long competitive career and has authored many books, one of which was made into the 2011 film Soul Surfer .

Christian Eriksen Returns to International & Premier League Play Following On-Pitch Cardiac Arrest

Some injuries are more than just career-altering. When footballer Christian Eriksen suffered a sudden cardiac arrest while playing for Denmark, it was a life-threatening situation.

The event occurred in June 2021, during Denmark's opening 2020 Euro match against Finland. Fortunately, medical personnel were able to revive him with CPR and an external defibrillator. He was later fitted with an Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (ICD)—a permanent medical device designed to regulate irregular heart rhythms.

Eriksen, who was signed to Inter Milan at the time, had his Serie A contract terminated because Italian sports regulations prohibited athletes from competing with an ICD. However, the frightening injury wouldn't keep Eriksen away from high-level competition.

The former Tottenham standout returned to the Premier League in early 2022 on a six-month contract with Brentford F.C. His first match back came as a substitute in a 2-0 defeat against Newcastle United, but it was still a successful return.

"If you take away the result, I'm one happy man," Eriksen said, per ESPN's Mark Ogden .

Eriksen also returned to international play in 2022 and represented Denmark at the 2022 FIFA World Cup. He has since had a four-year stint with Manchester United. He is currently signed to VfL Wolfsburg.

While Eriksen suffered a second cardiac event this past June while playing for Denmark, his ICD worked as intended. He was able to leave the pitch under his own power.

"As you can probably imagine, receiving a shock from my ICD has had a major effect on both me and my family, but I want to assure everyone that this was a different situation from what happened in 2021," Eriksen said, per the Associated Press .

Damar Hamlin Returns to NFL Following On-Field Cardiac Arrest

Like Eriksen, the Buffalo Bills safety endured a terrifying stretch when he suffered a cardiac arrest on the playing field. It occurred during a Monday Night Football game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The incident occurred in January 2023 and was the result of commotio cordis—a rare disruption of the heart's rhythm caused by a direct impact to the chest at a precise moment in the heart's electrical cycle.

Medical personnel were able to revive Hamlin with CPR and an external defibrillator. He was released from the hospital roughly a week later. Four and a half months after that, Hamlin was cleared to resume football activity.

The 2021 sixth-round pick out of Pitt made his return to the playing field during the 2023 preseason. His remarkable return for the regular season in 2023 was one of the most memorable sports storylines of the year, even if he only appeared in five games and somehow failed to win Comeback Player of the Year.

Hamlin was a full-time starter in 2024 and has remained on Buffalo's roster since making his triumphant return.

"I don't want to be just known as the player who lived," Hamlin told NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe in 2024. "My story is my story. It's still being written. But I want to be known for my abilities as well. I've always had big goals on and off the field. I have so much more that I want to accomplish."

Rafael Nadal Returns from Foot Injury to Win Australian Open

While Rafael Nadal might not be the GOAT of men's tennis, he's certainly on the short list. He retired at the conclusion of the 2024 season, but his legendary career nearly came to an abrupt end a few years earlier.

Nadal contemplated retirement in 2021 during a long layoff due to a serious, persistent foot injury.

"A lot of conversations with the team, with the family about what can happen or what's going to happen if the things continue like this, thinking that maybe is a chance to say goodbye," Nadal said of that stretch, per Tumaini Carayol of The Guardian .

However, Nadal returned to the court the following year and made history at the 2022 Australian Open.

In an epic showdown with Daniil Medvedev, Nadal battled back from a two-set deficit to claim victory in a match that lasted over five hours. The win gave Nadal his 21st Grand Slam title—a men's record at the time—and gave fans a truly memorable career highlight.

"If we put everything together, the scenario, the momentum, what it means. Yeah, without a doubt probably have been the biggest comeback of my tennis career," Nadal said, per Carayol .

Buster Posey Returns from Severe Leg Injury to Claim MVP and Batting Title

As a seven-time All-Star with three World Series championships on his resume, Buster Posey is probably a future Hall of Famer. (He'll be eligible in 2027.) One of the most memorable moments of his 12-season career came in 2012 following a significant leg injury.

In November 2011, Posey suffered a fractured fibula and three torn ankle ligaments during a home-plate collision against the Florida Marlins. However, he was back in the lineup for the San Francisco Giants' 2012 opener, albeit in a limited capacity.

"I put in a lot of work to get back in the game. Even though it was two innings, it was nice to be out there," Posey said following the 6-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, per Henry Schulman of SFGate.com.

While fans might not remember Posey's brief appearance in that 2012 opener, they certainly remember the historic season it helped spark.

Posey went on to appear in 148 games while earning the NL batting title and MVP honors. That led him to drive San Francisco to its second World Series title in three seasons.

Robert Kubica Returns to F1, Wins at Le Mans Following Devastating Crash

On Feb. 6, 2011, F1 driver Robert Kubica was involved in a devastating crash at the Ronde di Andora rally in Italy. His car struck a guardrail, which penetrated the vehicle and caused multiple significant injuries.

Along with fractures in his right arm, shoulder and leg, Kubica suffered a partial amputation of his right forearm. He faced permanent limitations in his right arm and hand that could easily have ended his racing career.

However, Kubica spent the next several years adapting to those limitations and training to race again. After first returning to rally racing, he made his official return to Formula One as a reserve driver in 2018 and became a full-time driver for Williams the following year.

"Now the difficult part begins," Kubica said in 2019, per Lawrence Barretto of Formula1.com.

With a 10th-place finish at the German Grand Prix, Kubica set a record for the largest gap (eight years and 256 days) between F1 championship-point finishes. He transitioned to endurance racing in 2021. In 2025, he won the 24 Hours of Le Mans as a member of the AF Corse team.

Kobe Bryant Returns from Multiple Injuries to Cap Career in Historic Fashion

The late, great Kobe Bryant provided many memorable moments during his legendary NBA career. One of the most enduring is how he finished it. He returned from three major injuries to give fans a fantastic farewell tour.

Bryant's career hit a significant roadblock on April 12, 2013, when he suffered a torn Achilles against the Golden State Warriors. He returned for six games in the 2013-14 season before suffering a left knee fracture against the Memphis Grizzlies.

Though Bryant returned for the 2014-15 season and played extremely well (22.3 points per game) for a 35-game stretch, he suffered a torn rotator cuff against the New Orleans Pelicans and finished his third straight season on the injured list.

Bryant returned yet again for the 2015-16 season and, in November of that year, announced via a poem in The Players' Tribune that he was embarking on his final campaign.

While Bryant's numbers in his final season didn't regularly match those of his prime, he started 66 games for the Los Angeles Lakers and played at an All-Star level, averaging 17.6 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.8 assists. He capped his farewell tour with one of the best final performances of all time .

Bryant walked off by dropping 60 on the Utah Jazz, with 23 points coming in the fourth quarter, in a 101-96 victory.

"It felt good to be able to do that one last time," Bryant told reporters after the game.

articles.title: Biggest Overreactions to NFL Week 1
articles.summary: Typically, there are major overreactions to Week 1 of the regular season. Many have opinions they've held since last year or based on the offseason.
articles.body:
Typically, there are major overreactions to Week 1 of the regular season. Many have opinions they've held since last year or based on the offseason.

Let's remember that the Las Vegas Raiders went on the road to beat the New England Patriots in Week 1 last year. The Raiders then won only two more games, and the Patriots advanced to the Super Bowl.

So, let's pump the brakes on potential playoff contenders and pretenders.

However, we can go through trending NFL takes that sound premature on a sample size of one game.

Here are seven overreactions to last week's contest and why they may be exaggerations.

Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase's Week 1 No-Show Is Concerning

Let's get the fantasy football angst out of the way.

For the first time since 2021, the Cincinnati Bengals scored more than 20 points in their season opener. Known for their slow starts, the Bengals finally bucked the trend and outscored the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 33-27, but Ja'Marr Chase stuck to the team's tradition of a quiet outing.

Chase hauled in two of just four targets for 12 yards. Given his recent knee injury , it's an alarming stat line, but he's been average or non-existent in Week 1 matchups over the previous few years (h/t Yahoo Sports):

After catching two passes for 26 yards in the Bengals' season opener against the Cleveland Browns last year, Chase followed up with 14 receptions for 165 yards and a touchdown, with backup quarterback Jake Browning playing through more than half of that game.

Chase didn't show any lingering effects from a recent knee injury. Still, Bengals fans and fantasy football managers need to be patient because in Week 2, Cincinnati plays the Houston Texans, who will look to redeem themselves following a poor defensive performance against the Buffalo Bills.

Chase may not post a gaudy stat line until he faces the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. Steelers' lead cornerback, Joey Porter Jr., is currently out with a back injury amid a contract dispute.

Cardinals Aren't One of the NFL's Worst Teams

The Arizona Cardinals ruined survivor pool picks with their upset win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Projected to have one of the lowest win totals of the season, the Cardinals likely used those predictions as bulletin-board material.

Regardless of the motivational source, the Cardinals earned an impressive victory, but let's not get carried away with their season outlook.

Arizona plays in arguably the league's toughest division, with the reigning Super Bowl champions, who will visit the Cardinals in Week 2, the Los Angeles Rams and the San Francisco 49ers, two perennial playoff contenders.

The Cardinals didn't win a divisional matchup last season, and they may not win one this year. Moreover, outside of the NFC West, Arizona has games against the Detroit Lions, Philadelphia Eagles and the Kansas City Chiefs with a healthy Patrick Mahomes.

Credit to the Cardinals for beating the Chargers, who are perpetual underachievers. But it's going to take more than one impressive win to change the expectations for a rebuilding team with bridge-gap quarterback Jacoby Brissett.

Panthers Wasted Cap Space on Defensive Free Agents

According to ESPN Insights , the Carolina Panthers gave up the second-most points (59) in an NFL season opener. The Chicago Bears ran for 291 yards and six touchdowns against the Panthers' new-look front seven.

This offseason, Carolina signed edge-rusher Jaelan Phillips to a four-year, $120 million deal, inked Pro Bowl linebacker Devin Lloyd to a three-year, $42 million contract, added linebacker Bobby Okereke on a one-year, $1.5 million pact and drafted defensive tackle Lee Hunter in the second round.

All four of those defenders made solid contributions in Sunday's loss to the Bears, but it wasn't enough to slow down one of the league's most electric offenses.

Carolina's 59-37 loss says more about Chicago's offense than its defensive unit.

Last season, the Panthers' defense ranked 27th in scoring and total yards. They needed to add potential upgrades on that side of the ball. Carolina's defense will improve, but it faced a juggernaut last Sunday.

The Seattle Seahawks made Drake Maye look like a below-average quarterback in his last two games. He's thrown three touchdown passes and five interceptions between Super Bowl LX and Week 1 of this season.

The Patriots seemed poised to avenge their 29-13 loss to the Seahawks, leading for most of the season opener up until the fourth quarter. With possession in the red zone on the final drive of the contest, Maye threw an inexcusable pass in the end zone, and Josh Jobe picked it off to seal the win for Seattle.

If Maye threw the ball out of bounds, kicker Andre Borregales could've had a chip-shot field-goal attempt to push the game into overtime, but his turnover completed New England's fourth-quarter meltdown.

After the game, many questioned if Maye could play up to heightened expectations after he finished the 2025 campaign as the runner-up for league MVP. Critics believe a tougher schedule will expose him.

As a third-year pro with 30 career starts, Maye still has a high ceiling with room for growth. He'll learn from his mistakes. Even without wideout A.J. Brown, the 24-year-old signal-caller should be able to bounce back with Romeo Doubs, though he struggled with drops last week, Mack Hollins, Hunter Henry and rookie third-rounder Eli Raridon, who scored a touchdown against the Seahawks.

Expect Maye to be sharper at home against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2.

Raiders Can Build Offensive Momentum Without Brock Bowers

With a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins, the Las Vegas Raiders had their highest scoring output since Week 18 of the 2023 season. Former Raider linebacker and team broadcaster Kirk Morrison noted that the club didn't score 17 points in a half of any game last season, but it did last Sunday against the Dolphins.

Given that Brock Bowers missed the previous game while recovering from a meniscus trim, the Raiders should feel encouraged by their offensive output, but they still need their All-Pro tight end.

Bowers' presence alone opens up the passing attack for his teammates because he commands help coverage downfield.

Although the Raiders scored 27 points against a rebuilding Dolphins squad, Kirk Cousins only threw for 160 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. None of Las Vegas' pass-catchers eclipsed 45 receiving yards. The top three wideouts, Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, all had two or three catches.

The Raiders can decisively beat the Dolphins without Bowers, but they need him to breathe life into their passing attack against stiffer competition.

Rams 2026 Dream Team Will Be a Disappointment

The Los Angeles Rams, who have the best odds (+600) to win Super Bowl LXI via FanDuel , went to Australia and laid an egg in a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

The Rams arrived in Australia on game day, but their unorthodox travel schedule doesn't excuse a 20-point loss to a division rival.

Defensive tackle Aaron Donald didn't suit up for the game, and edge rusher Myles Garrett was on and off the field, managing a knee injury that sidelined him for offseason practices. According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the Rams placed Garrett on injured reserve after he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, though he could return in four weeks.

Many of you remember the Philadelphia Eagles' 2011 dream team that went 8-8 and missed the playoffs, but the Rams won't share that fate.

Before the Rams acquired Garrett and welcomed back Donald from retirement, they were Super Bowl contenders. Moreover, with Donald's eventual return, the Rams' next opponent, the New York Giants, probably won't run for nearly 200 yards against them as the 49ers did.

Under head coach Sean McVay, the Rams have won at least 10 games in three consecutive seasons—a 10-7 record is the floor for this team. Los Angeles will rebound and refuel its Super Bowl buzz in a home matchup against the Giants next Monday night.

Texans Defense Is Headed for Significant Regression

In 2025, the Houston Texans didn't allow more than 30 points in any of their games, including the playoffs. In their season opener, they gave up 36 points in a loss to the Buffalo Bills, whom they held to 19 points last year.

Did Buffalo figure out Houston's defense and provide a blueprint for the rest of the league? In short, no.

Few teams have a quarterback comparable to Josh Allen, the 2024 league MVP and a four-time Pro Bowler. He threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two scores against the Texans.

Houston faced a superstar signal-caller who made some spectacular plays with his arm and legs, but don't expect that to be the norm against this top-tier defensive unit.

In 2025, the Texans defense allowed the second-fewest points and the fewest yards. That unit still features four defensive backs who recorded four interceptions and two pass-rushers who logged 12-plus sacks in the previous campaign. This offseason, Houston added safety Reed Blankenship, who recorded four interceptions in 2024.

The Texans defense should own the majority blame for the team's loss to the Bills, but it's still a loaded group with several defenders who can make game-changing plays. Good luck to any team that doesn't have Allen or Lamar Jackson under center.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: NFL Week 1 takeaways: Bengals flash contender upside, Bears explode and Packers collapse
articles.summary: From the Bengals' dominant defense to the Bills' 96-yard game-winning drive in Houston, every NFL Week 1 game produced an interesting storyline.
articles.body: I love the NFL and I don't care who knows it. As sad as I am to see summer coming to an end, I couldn't be more excited that the best league on the planet is back and in full swing. As you might imagine, I have some thoughts about the first Sunday of the NFL season. Below, you will find my biggest takeaway from each game. Bengals 33, Buccaneers 27 Takeaway: If the Cincinnati Bengals defense is actually this good, this team is a top-five Super Bowl contender. Yes, the Bucs scored 27 points. But that total is misleading: Tampa Bay’s defense scored on a pick-six, and the offense’s final touchdown came against a prevent defense with Cincinnati leading by two scores. The Bengals held Tampa Bay to 282 yards and forced four turnovers. If the defense is legit and Burrow stays healthy (he was sacked just once, another major positive), Cincinnati is extremely dangerous. FORMER NAVY MIDSHIPMAN LANDON ROBINSON SHOWS UP TO HIS FIRST NFL GAME IN FULL DRESS MILITARY UNIFORM Lions 31, Saints 30 Takeaway: There’s no reason for Detroit to panic over a near-historic second-half collapse because the Saints might actually be good. Obviously, blowing a 21-0 second-half lead is less than ideal. But Tyler Shough threw for 410 yards, Chris Olave played out of his mind and New Orleans erased that deficit despite committing three turnovers. Detroit still ran for 165 yards, sacked Shough five times and stopped the potential game-winning 2-point conversion. The Lions' secondary is a concern, but that comeback probably says more about New Orleans than it does about Detroit. Jets 23, Titans 10 Takeaway: It’s going to be a long year in Tennessee. Tennessee was outgained 367-195 at home by a Jets team starting Geno Smith at quarterback. The Titans had 112 yards through three quarters, and Cam Ward’s only touchdown came in garbage time. Robert Saleh inherited a bad roster, but neither side of the ball offered much reason for optimism. The Jets might be better than expected, but Tennessee still looks like one of the worst teams in football. Ravens 41, Colts 23 Takeaway: Derrick Henry continues to defy all laws of physics, gravity and aging in the NFL. Henry is 32 years old, plays the most punishing position in football and just ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns. His second score moved him past Marcus Allen into third place on the NFL’s all-time rushing touchdown list, behind only LaDainian Tomlinson and Emmitt Smith. Baltimore gained 506 yards and simply overpowered Indianapolis whenever it wanted. At some point Henry has to slow down. Right? Steelers 20, Falcons 13 Takeaway: Well, one team had to win this game, but neither should be excited about their performance. Neither offense produced more than 264 yards or 13 points; T.J. Watt supplied Pittsburgh's second touchdown with a pick-six. The Falcons at least have the excuse that the two quarterbacks who were expected to start games this season, Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., missed the game with injuries. The Steelers got the win, but the offense was basically at full strength and didn't look impressive at all. I don't know how either fan base can feel good about this one. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Bears 59, Panthers 37 Takeaway: The Bears offense is definitely going to be good, but temper expectations after a clear outlier performance. Caleb Williams accounted for four touchdowns, and the Bears had two 100-yard rushers. D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai combined for 224 yards on the ground and four scores. That’s absurd production, regardless of opponent. This was the highest-scoring season opener in NFL history, so anyone expecting the Bears to regularly post 50+ points is overreacting to a historic performance. Still, Ben Johnson has too many weapons for this offense not to finish among the NFL’s best. Jaguars 34, Browns 10 Takeaway: Deshaun Watson has no business being a starting NFL quarterback. It feels like Browns owner Jimmy Haslam is determined to get some value from the worst trade in NFL history, but it's a lost cause. As a businessman, Haslam should understand the concept of a "sunk cost." Watson is terrible, even if his final stat line doesn’t tell the whole story (and it doesn't, and not even half of it). His third pass was intercepted and turned into a Jacksonville touchdown, Cleveland fell behind 31-0 and his lone scoring pass was a 46-yarder with 1:52 remaining. Not only that, but he looked completely lost. I'm not the biggest Shedeur Sanders fan, but there's no reason he shouldn't be starting (or even Dillon Gabriel, for that matter). Bills 36, Texans 31 Takeaway: The biggest win of the day belongs to the Bills, who look like a good bet to reach the AFC Championship Game. Buffalo went on the road against one of the AFC’s best defenses, trailed in the fourth quarter and responded with a 96-yard game-winning drive. Josh Allen accounted for four touchdowns and won in Houston for the first time in five tries. The Bills defense then sealed the victory with a strip-sack after the Texans reached the Buffalo 9-yard line. That’s how a legitimate AFC contender wins a football game. Raiders 27, Dolphins 13 Takeaway: It’s going to be an even longer season in Miami than it is in Tennessee. The Raiders gained only 290 yards and Kirk Cousins threw two interceptions, yet Miami never seriously threatened to win the game. The Dolphins went 2-of-10 on third down, allowed five sacks, gained only 259 yards, picked up just 13 first downs and scored one offensive touchdown. At least Tennessee is rebuilding around a young quarterback. What exactly is Miami building? CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Vikings 39, Packers 22 Takeaway: The Packers need to figure out why they can’t protect second-half leads, and they need to figure it out now. Green Bay led 22-10 in the third quarter against Carson Wentz, who was playing only because Kyler Murray was nearly decapitated in the first quarter. The Packers kicked a field goal that would have given them a 25-17 lead, but they accepted an offsides penalty on Minnesota, took the points off the board and then failed on fourth-and-1. Ultimately, Minnesota scored the game’s final 29 points. The Packers have now lost the last three games in which they held a double-digit second-half lead: Week 16 against Chicago, the Wild Card rematch with the Bears and Sunday against Minnesota. Once is a fluke. Twice is concerning. Three times, all against division rivals, is a catastrophe of epic proportions. Eagles 24, Commanders 22 Takeaway: This might sound strange, but Commanders fans should be more encouraged by this game than Eagles fans. This isn’t to say Washington should celebrate a loss because they shouldn’t. But the Commanders went on the road against a supposed NFC contender and came one 2-point conversion from overtime after an injury-ravaged five-win season. Philadelphia can bank the victory, but its repeated second-half three-and-outs (the Eagles had only 10 first downs the entire game) did nothing to prove that last season’s inconsistency is gone. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Cardinals 26, Chargers 14 Takeaway: I’m trying not to overreact, but man did the Chargers look awful. Arizona entered Sunday on a nine-game losing streak, started Jacoby Brissett on the road and completely dominated the second half. The Cardinals blocked a punt, intercepted Justin Herbert and held Los Angeles to just 117 yards of offense in the second half. Mike McDaniel’s offense was supposed to unlock even more from Herbert, but it produced only two scoring drives, and one was aided by a 48-yard penalty. It’s only one game, but no "contender" looked worse. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Giants 28, Cowboys 20 Takeaway: John Harbaugh built an all-star coaching staff in New York, and it showed on "Sunday Night Football." All offseason, Dallas was treated as the team most likely to challenge Philadelphia in the NFC East. Maybe everyone picked the wrong team. Harbaugh surrounded himself with former head coaches and longtime coordinators, and the Giants looked better prepared, more physical and more complete than Dallas in Week 1. Jaxson Dart looked comfortable, the defense gave Dak Prescott fits and, if the Giants can keep their stars healthy, New York suddenly looks capable of pushing for its first division title since 2011.

articles.title: Stefon Diggs guilty of NFL's dumbest move of Week 1 and it may have decided Commanders loss to Eagles
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs jumped on the goal post after scoring against the Philadelphia Eagles, drawing a 15-yard penalty that prevented a key two-point try.
articles.body: The dumbest thing any NFL player did in Week 1 of the regular season? That was Stefon Diggs, who was guilty of a clownish touchdown celebration that cost his team – perhaps dearly. Diggs, 32, is one of the league's most-gifted route runners. He's elite in that respect and he showed it on a 10-yard touchdown in Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Diggs made Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean think he was going one way, and then went the other way, leaving him wide open for the score. NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS But then Diggs showed everyone perhaps the reason he's playing for his fourth team in four years when he completely lost his mind after the score. Diggs, you see, celebrated his first touchdown with his new team by jumping on the goal post. It's an old Antonio Brown celebration from more than a decade ago. The NFL calls it using the goal post as a prop which is against the rules. So Diggs was immediately flagged for the foolish move. "As soon as I wrapped my arms around it I was like this: 'Oh I forgot,'" Diggs told reporters at his locker stall after the game. "Back in the day, you know, I've been playing a long time, you used to could do that. "So, update on the rules and sometimes when you've been in the game a long time, uh, I got to be better." SAINTS DEFENSE HAS TOUCHDOWN TAKEN AWAY AGAINST LIONS AFTER JARED GOFF FUMBLE IS STUNNINGLY OVERTURNED To be clear, there has never been a time when Diggs, who entered the league in 2015, could do this and not be penalized. Using the goal post as a prop became illegal in 2006. Anyway, no biggie right? Wrong. Diggs might have helped cost his team the game because of his celebration. He certainly cost his team the opportunity to tie the game. The Commanders trailed 17-9 with 10 minutes left in the game before Diggs scored. So his TD made it 17-15. Washington coach Dan Quinn would have been right to follow the Diggs score by trying to tie the game with a two-point attempt. Indeed, that was his intention. "Yeah, we were going to go for two," the coach said afterward. Apart from the 15-yard penalty Diggs incurred for his tomfoolery prevented the Commanders from trying that game-tying 2-point attempt from the 2-yard line. The Commanders had to kick the extra point instead to make the game, 17-16. Did we mention the Commanders lost the game, 24-22? The inability to go for 2 points after the Diggs score to tie the game forced the Commanders to try a 2-pointer later. They failed on that conversion which would have been moot if they could have converted the 2-point try after the Diggs score. An extra point later would have tied the game at 24. No worries. A team is a brotherhood and Diggs was excused for his antics, right? Nope. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "You’ve just got to be smarter," quarterback Jayden Daniels lamented. "We got to know situations and situational football ... We’ve just got to be smart. There is a time and place for everything and celebrations. I'm pretty sure at that point we could have gone for two." Daniels actually blamed himself for not reminding the other players in the huddle to avoid doing dumb stuff if they scored. But who could have predicted someone humping the goal post? "I did have a conversation with [Diggs] about that," Quinn said. Yes, but that talk came after the fact. "He knows better in that space and he knows that," Quinn added. "So we did talk about that in that spot. I love his fight. I love what he stands for, but as the competitor, he knows better in that spot." Apparently Diggs didn't know. And it cost his team. articles.title: How Justin Herbert turned a $262 million contract into a financial empire before turning 30
articles.summary: NFL News: Justin Herbert is 28 years old, still under contract with the Los Angeles Chargers, and already sitting on a financial portfolio that most athletes do.
articles.body: Justin Herbert is 28 years old, still under contract with the Los Angeles Chargers, and already sitting on a financial portfolio that most athletes don't build in an entire career. His net worth currently stands at $40 million, backed by a five-year, $262.5 million extension signed in July 2023 that includes $218 million in guaranteed money and an average annual salary of $52.5 million. And that's just the salary side of the ledger. The off-field story is what most people overlook.What is Justin Herbert's net worth in 2026?Justin Herbert's net worth is estimated at $40 million as of 2026, with an annual salary of $52 million from his Chargers deal. But those numbers alone don't tell the full story of how quickly his wealth has grown. In 2020, he earned $17.6 million. By 2022, that dropped to $3 million as his rookie deal structure played out. Then in 2025, it surged to $60 million -- the year his new-money contract kicked in at full force.What's striking is the speed of accumulation. In 2025 alone, Herbert received $100 million as part of how the contract was structured in its first new-money year. That kind of front-loading, combined with a no-trade clause and near-total guarantees, is not just a quarterback payday. It's financial architecture. The Chargers essentially gave Herbert the leverage to plan his wealth-building on his own timeline, not the league's.Herbert climbed to No. 3 on Forbes' Highest-Paid NFL Players list in 2025, with Forbes estimating his total earnings at $71 million that year. For a quarterback who has yet to win a Super Bowl, that standing says something about how the market values his ceiling -- not just his resume.How does Justin Herbert make money beyond his NFL salary?The contract is the headline. The endorsements are the compounding interest.Herbert has active deals with Nike, Bose, Head and Shoulders, FedEx, and Chipotle, among others. Nike came first -- and it came early. He signed with the brand ahead of the 2020 NFL Draft, becoming one of its youngest NFL faces at the time, with the Oregon connection to Nike going back decades. He has since added deals with Fanatics, Panini America, Lowe's, Hyundai, and SoFi, the last of which is particularly telling. Partnering with a financial services company while still in your mid-twenties signals a deliberate effort to be taken seriously off the field.Herbert described his approach to brand alignment plainly: "I've been very happy with my endorsements... I feel comfortable with [these brands] and feel they represent me well." That's not an athlete taking every available check. That's someone being selective, which tends to hold brand value longer.The profile of his sponsorship portfolio, spread across tech, retail, food, and financial services, suggests he's not chasing celebrity exposure. He's building brand equity across industries.How does Justin Herbert's personal life factor into his financial profile?Herbert announced his engagement to pop singer Madison Beer on July 28, 2026, in a joint Instagram post captioned simply: "meet my fiancé." The ring alone became a news story — experts estimated the engagement ring, described as featuring an elongated cushion cut of over 15 carats, to be worth anywhere between $700,000 and $1.2 million.Beyond the optics, the engagement put two very different financial trajectories in the spotlight. Beer, a Forbes 30 Under 30 alumna with a Grammy nomination for her 2026 album "Locket," has an estimated net worth of $18 million. Together, the couple's combined net worth is estimated at nearly $74 million.What matters here is context. Beer's career is on an upward curve -- her latest album debuted in the Billboard 200 Top 10, and her profile has grown considerably through 2025 and 2026. Herbert, meanwhile, is entering his seventh NFL season with three more years left on a fully guaranteed deal. Both are in growth phases simultaneously. The combined financial picture is likely to look considerably different by the time Herbert's contract expires in 2029.For a quarterback from Eugene, Oregon who entered the league as the sixth overall pick with modest fanfare, the arc is genuinely unusual. The money is large. The endorsements are strategic. And at 28, Herbert hasn't even entered the peak years of what quarterbacks typically earn.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Pissed Off,' Dak Prescott Reacts to Cowboys' Loss to Jaxson Dart, Giants in NFL Week 1 Rivalry Game
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys opened the 2026 season with a 28-20 loss against the NFC East rival New York Giants on Sunday Night Football, and their players are not happy about it.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys opened the 2026 season with a 28-20 loss against the NFC East rival New York Giants on Sunday Night Football , and their players are not happy about it.

After the game, Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott told reporters that he and his teammates are "pissed off" about their disappointing primetime performance.

Prescott threw for just 175 yards, two touchdowns and an interception on 22-of-34 passing in Sunday night's loss. He was outplayed by Giants second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart, who finished with 230 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions while completing 23 of his 29 passes. Dallas also totaled just 69 rushing yards, while New York racked up 165 yards on the ground.

In addition to the lackluster production, the Cowboys also showed a lack of discipline. Dallas committed eight penalties that cost the team 85 yards. When running back Javonte Williams caught a 17-yard touchdown pass from Prescott in the fourth quarter, he committed a taunting penalty that led to Brandon Aubrey missing the ensuing extra point, which would've made it a seven-point game.

"Overall as a football team, we were pretty poor," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the game . "That's certainly not our standard. We certainly didn't come out of the gate fast enough on either side of the ball. This is a humbling business, and we got humbled."

The Cowboys were hoping to return to playoff contention after missing the postseason in each of the last two years, but Sunday's performance shows they have a lot of work to do before they can keep up with the elite teams in the NFC.

Dallas will try to get back on track in Week 2 with another NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders, who also lost their season opener against the rival Philadelphia Eagles.

First-year offensive coordinator Matt Nagy drew up a game plan that played perfectly to Dart's strengths.

The Minnesota Vikings' 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers was one of Sunday's most surprising scores for two reasons. Starting quarterback Kyler Murray exited after just 11 plays, and Minnesota was down 22-10 midway through the third quarter.

Backup quarterback Carson Wentz and a ball-hawking defense inspired quite the second-half comeback. The Vikings' final three touchdowns all came within the final 6:37 of the game.

Altogether, Week 1 set a high bar for the rest of the season to follow.

articles.title: Four Downs: The 4 pivotal plays that determined Cowboys’ 28-20 loss to Giants
articles.summary: The Cowboys opened their 2026 NFL season with a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants on SNF. Here are the 4 most pivotal downs that unraveled it all.
articles.body:
Similar to the season that came before, the Dallas Cowboys began this new football year with a crippling division loss. Falling to the New York Giants , 28-20, Dallas provided a masterclass in unforced errors and defensive ineptitude.

By the time Dak Prescott and the vaunted offense found its rhythm, it was too late. Despite scoring touchdowns on every possession of the second half, the Dallas defense couldn't stop Jaxon Dart 's offense down the stretch.

It was a game made up of penalties, miscues, and unmatched physicality. But four downs in particular, served as pivotal moments in the Cowboys' opening week loss to the Giants. They were four plays that deserve further attention. Some of those plays need to be addressed and corrected, but some are just some good, old fashioned bad luck.

With the score tied 7-7 in the second quarter, the Cowboys were fresh off a fumble recovery to steal possession, and hopefully, tip the balance. In a 2 nd -and-4 situation following a 6-yard run by Javonte Williams , Prescott aired it out to George Pickens deep down the sideline. Pickens dropped a perfectly placed ball.

The play itself didn't represent a monumental shift in momentum or win percentage, but what followed four plays later was a tide turner, of which, the Cowboys never recovered. It was here, with less than a minute remaining in the half, where Prescott threw his only interception of the afternoon.

While Prescott deserves all the blame in the world for his reckless turnover, it was a moment that was made possible by the tremendous missed opportunity just a few plays before.

Just in case anyone was feeling nostalgic for the Matt Eberflus era, Christian Parker did his best to offer up a familiar sight to fans as the first half drew to a close. With just 58 seconds on the clock, the Cowboys allowed the Giants to pick apart their soft zone coverage all the way to paydirt. It was the touchdown play in particular that was the icing on the cake.

On 2 nd -and-5 with 25 seconds to go, Dart hit Isaiah Likely for a 15-yard touchdown on a blown coverage. In what appeared to be quarters coverage with MOD (man outside and deep) responsibilities, no one bothered to cover Likely as he broke to the outside corner of the endzone. The play resulted in a 3.0 EPA for New York, setting the Giants up to "double-dip" as they scored touchdowns to close the first half and open the second half.

Down No. 3: Sometimes the way the ball bounces

Luck wasn't on the Cowboys' side Week 1 either. With the score 21-14, in New York's favor, Cam Skattebo fumbled the ball at the 12:04 mark of the third quarter. Bouncing directly back into his wantful arms, he recovered his own drop, collecting a first down and 1.1 in EPA in the process. DeMarvion Overshown was also injured on the play.

Instead of being a change of possession, this drive sustained and scored, eating up clock and allowing the Cowboys offense only two possessions in the second half. The Cowboys forced four fumbles on the night, but only recovered one. This final almost-turnover had the largest consequences.

Headlining what could be a weekly series titled, "What were you thinking?" Javonte Williams committed what could have been a catastrophic penalty when he taunted his way to the endzone running in a 17-yard touchdown reception with 5:26 remaining in the fourth. His 15-yard penalty resulted in a missed extra point by Brandon Aubrey , keeping Dallas behind by eight.

If the Cowboys would have stopped New York on their final drive – which of course, they didn't – this would have been one more enormous hurdle for the Cowboys to overcome. Not only would they have to drive the length of the field for a touchdown, but they'd have to score a 2-point conversion just to tie the game. With a conversion rate of just 41 percent in the NFL, a 2-point conversion is not an ideal situation to put one's team.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 1 Game vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Welp. Any optimism for the Cleveland Browns took a major hit in Week 1 with the Browns falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-10 in the season opener.
articles.body:
Welp. Any optimism for the Cleveland Browns took a major hit in Week 1 with the Browns falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-10 in the season opener.

The beginning of the Todd Monken era could best be described as disastrous. It started with a Deshaun Watson interception on the opening drive and was compounded by a defense that couldn't seem to cover the Jaguars passing attack all afternoon.

It was a performance that the Browns would like to flush and move on from heading into another road game against Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers next week.

Woof. Deshaun Watson's debut could not have gone worse. The box score doesn't quite capture how bad he was. A 46-yard heave to rookie Denzel Boston and some other garbage time completions made the final stat line look better than he actually played.

Watson missed open receivers on multiple occasions, set the tone with a terrible interception on the first drive and took five sacks.

Watson didn't handle pressure well and he shared part of the blame for all the pressure he faced. The pick on the first drive was a terrible decision, it was followed by a three-and-out then a strip sack resulted in a punt on the third drive.

With the Jaguars scoring on the first three possessions, Watson's rocky start was a major reason this game was over as soon as it got started.

Judkins was largely shut down on the day. Some of that was the offensive line. He had 33 rushing yards but never got more than five yards on a carry.

The second-year back's biggest gain of the afternoon came on a 16-yard swing pass when the game was well out of hand in the fourth quarter.

Raheim Sanders got some run after Dylan Sampson was injured early in the game. He only had one carry, but he chipped in three receptions for 25 yards. He also showed some juice in the return game which was nice to see.

The veteran leader of this group wasn't really a leader at all. He was open on a comeback route that would have helped his statline if Watson hadn't airmailed it to the sideline, but bringing in two of four targets for 26 yards doesn't cut it.

The first-round rookie was a key contributor to the Browns ugly start. His second reception killed the second drive when he lost a fumble. Still, he caught four of his five targets and had a nice 25-yard catch over Jourdan Lewis. He also had the team's longest run at 10 yards.

Boston's grade here comes with an asterisk because he was mostly a non-factor early on. However, it's worth acknowledging that his first catch was a 13-yarder that moved the sticks on second-and-13 and the 46 yard touchdown is one of the few highlights the Browns can feel good about coming out of Sunday.

Fantasy managers won't be happy about Fannin's output. He had just two catches for 12 yards, but those yards all came on a dump off when Watson was under pressure. Fannin did a good job to lower his shoulder and get a few extra yards, but there wasn't much to write home about here.

Whiteheart registered the first catch of the season for the Browns when Watson connected with him on the first drive. The Browns didn't do enough in the run game to believe Whiteheart was a difference maker there, either.

The Browns first pick of the 2026 draft drew a tough assignment in his first game. Cleveland chipped Josh Hines-Allen and Fano still lost the rep to him on Hines-Allen's half-sack. Although, it should be noted that Watson's dropback on the play didn't help him.

Johnson's first game with the Browns was rough. He had two holding penalties that set the offense back and was part of the reason the running game created little daylight for Judkins.

There wasn't much to say about Jenkins performance. The center was not at fault for much of the pressure Watson faced, but he also didn't do anything to get a higher grade.

Austin Barber is the solution for anyone looking for positives from the offense on Sunday. Starting for an injured Teven Jenkins, the third-round pick held his own against the Jags defensive front and was the Browns' highest-graded player by PFF .

Howard is supposed to be the veteran leader of this group, but his false start came after one of Johnson's holdings and contributed to a first-and-30 situation. Travon Walker had 1.5 sacks, a tackle for a loss and quarterback hit.

Jared Verse got a tough lesson in what it looks like to be a team's premier pass-rusher. He was chipped and double-teamed much more than he was in Los Angeles and became a non-factor as a pass-rusher.

Verse was at least drawing additional attention from the Jaguars scheme. McGuire should have been the beneficiary, but registered just one pressure on 16 reps.

McGuire might not have been great, but Williams didn't do anything to command more of his reps. He worked as the team's rotational edge-rusher and didn't stand out on a bad defensive day.

Mason Graham was one of the few bright spots on Sunday. He was lined up across from rookie Emmanuel Pregnon and took full advantage. He accounted for two of the Browns' four tackles for a loss and beat Robert Hainsey for the only sack of the day.

Huntington is never going to be a player that shows up in the box score. He registered just two tackles, but he also struggled to hold up at the point of attack and win his gap. The Jaguars were able to run the ball whenever they wanted to and Huntington was part of the problem.

Hall registered the same amount of snaps as Huntington (29), but was also not impactful. The Jaguars won the matchups on the interior that did not involve Graham.

Collins' was a rotational piece, but the veteran made a case to play a bit more moving forward. He had some juice coming off the ball and was right behind Graham on his sack.

The box score will tell you that Carson Schwesinger led the Browns with 10 tackles, but he also had a coverage blunder that led to a Brenton Strange touchdown. Only three of his tackles were solo and one was for a loss.

Schwesinger was still the best inside linebacker. Williams was not all that active with just four tackles despite playing every snap of the game.

Nobody from the secondary deserves a mark higher than a B. There were lapses in communication and coverage that cost the Browns all afternoon. However, Ward was simply beat by Josh Cameron on a slant for the second touchdown of the day.

Campbell was beaten multiple times as Trevor Lawrence racked up a passer rating of 150.6. He was notably late to break on a comeback route from Parker Washington and looked lost in zone coverage on more than one occasion.

It was clear that picking on Myles Harden was part of the Jaguars gameplan. He gave up the first touchdown to Washington and Lawrence did not stop finding who he was supposed to be covering the whole day.

Again, it's hard to give anyone in the defensive backfield glowing reviews. The coverage was bad overall, but Delpit had some good moments. He broke up a Parker Washington target at one point and played relatively good coverage when targeted.

The best thing you can say for Hickman is that he made some tackles when Jacksonville's run game got to the third level. His coverage wasn't stellar, though.

Hey, at least the kicker made the 26-yard field goal and his lone extra point attempt.

Bojorquez only punted three times thanks to the Browns turnover issues. One was downed inside the 20 and he averaged 43.3 yards.

Sanders looked like he should be more involved in the offensive gameplan ripping off a 74-yard kick return.

articles.title: NFL Week 1: Most controversial calls from Sunday’s games
articles.summary: Sunday’s NFL games brought some officiating controversies, including disputed penalties, missed calls, replay decisions and game-changing no-calls.
articles.body:
The NFL Week 1 schedule concludes Monday night when the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos , but Sunday's action already produced several controversial officiating decisions.

Not every questionable call made this list. Some penalties were obvious and correctly called. The focus here is on decisions or non-calls that generated significant debate, particularly when they affected scoring opportunities or potentially changed the momentum of a game.

Here are some of the most controversial officiating moments from Week 1 so far.

Giants' Cam Skattebo left frustrated after facemask no-call

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44). Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The New York Giants also benefited from a controversial no-call against the Dallas Cowboys .

In the second quarter, Giants running back Cam Skattebo was tackled on third-and-2 when Dallas defensive tackle Quinnen Williams appeared to grab his facemask and pull his head backward.

Officials did not throw a flag. Skattebo immediately showed his frustration with the officials and was left with a bloody nose after the play. The no-call ended the Giants' possession, making it particularly frustrating for New York even though the Giants eventually defeated Dallas 28-20.

Saints lose defensive touchdown after controversial replay

The New Orleans Saints appeared to take a defensive touchdown off Jared Goff 's fumble during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions .

With 9:34 remaining in the second quarter, Goff was facing third-and-16 from Detroit's 32-yard line when Saints defensive end Chase Young got around the edge and hit him as he began his throwing motion. The ball traveled backward, and New Orleans safety Jonas Sanker recovered it before returning it for a touchdown.

Officials initially ruled it a fumble and touchdown, but replay overturned the call and ruled Goff's pass incomplete. The decision sparked immediate frustration because the ball clearly traveled backward.

The NFL's rule interpretation supported the reversal because Goff had begun his throwing motion before contact. Still, the unusual ruling became one of the most debated calls of the weekend, particularly because New Orleans lost 31-30 in overtime.

Packers flagged repeatedly during Vikings' go-ahead drive

Green Bay Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd (32) against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images.

The Green Bay Packers had several calls go against them during the Minnesota Vikings' fourth-quarter comeback, with three defensive penalties keeping Minnesota's go-ahead touchdown drive alive.

The Vikings trailed 22-17 early in the fourth quarter when Green Bay's Jordan Love was stopped on fourth-and-1. Minnesota then began a 111-yard scoring drive.

Jonathan Ford was first flagged for encroachment. Later, Javon Bullard was called for illegal contact, wiping out a third-down sack. Rookie Chris McClellan was then penalized for a late hit on Carson Wentz after an incompletion.

The biggest controversy came with 6:49 remaining. Evan Williams intercepted Wentz in the end zone, apparently ending the drive, but Xavier McKinney was called for defensive holding. The interception was erased, and Aaron Jones scored on the next play.

Packers coverage questioned several of the calls, particularly McClellan's late-hit penalty and McKinney's holding call. Green Bay ultimately finished with 12 penalties for 98 yards.

Packers also get no-call on Justin Jefferson facemask

The Packers had another officiating complaint during the same fourth-quarter drive.

With Minnesota moving toward the end zone, Justin Jefferson appeared to have his facemask grabbed on a play that could have given the Vikings a first-and-goal from the Green Bay 3-yard line.

The Vikings eventually scored the go-ahead touchdown on Aaron Jones' 3-yard run, turning the sequence into one of the most scrutinized stretches of the game.

Eagles' touchdown survives potential false-start call

The Philadelphia Eagles also faced questions over a missed false-start call against the Washington Commanders .

Washington coach Dan Quinn said after the game that officials did not call what he believed was a false start on an Eagles touchdown play. Quinn specifically said he received no explanation for why the penalty was not called.

The decision became more significant because Philadelphia's 24-22 victory ultimately came down to Washington's failed two-point conversion attempt late in the fourth quarter.

articles.title: 4 eye-opening observations from Eagles' Week 1 win over Commanders
articles.summary: Here are a few more takeaways following the Eagles' Week 1 victory that you're certain to find interesting.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles won't earn style points for Sunday's 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders , but they earned something far more important. They earned a win, an early tie-breaker over the Commanders , and momentum to carry them into Week 2.

Philadelphia's season opener was equal parts encouraging and frustrating. The offense showed flashes and offered cause for concern. The defense delivered timely plays despite running out of gas after spending too much time on the field.

The special teams unit contributed winning moments. Kudos are for Braden Mann , the punter. Most importantly, the win gives an early share of the lead in the NFC East race. As the dust settles, several interesting nuggets emerged from Sunday's victory.

Jalen Hurts and Nick Sirianni are now 6-0 in Week 1

The Eagles have developed a habit of starting fast under Nick Sirianni. Sunday's victory improved Sirianni and Jalen Hurts to 6-0 in season openers together, a remarkable accomplishment considering how difficult it can be to navigate Week 1 uncertainty.

Hurts has now thrown for 1,310 yards, nine touchdowns, and two interceptions in season openers. He has scored 12 total touchdowns and boasts a 98.2 passer rating. The win also placed Sirianni in rare company. Only five head coaches in NFL history have won each of their first six career season openers: Potsy Clark, George Allen, Mike Shanahan, Jim Harbaugh and Sirianni.

Nick Sirianni continues to excel in close games.

For all the criticism he occasionally receives, Sirianni's teams continue to be ready when the games begin to count. The Eagles have made a habit of testing their fans' blood pressure. Fortunately for Philadelphia, they have also made a habit of winning close games under Sirianni.

Sunday's two-point victory added another chapter to an already impressive résumé. Sirianni now owns a 35-14 record in one-score games, giving him the third-best winning percentage in one-score contests in NFL history. That's not luck. That's a pattern.

Good coaches find ways to navigate chaos. Great coaches consistently come out on the winning side. Whether it's clock management, situational football, or maintaining composure in pressure-packed moments, Sirianni's teams have repeatedly shown they can finish games. Sunday provided another example.

Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell were all over the field

The Eagles entered the season believing they had one of the NFL's most athletic linebacker duos. Week 1 offered plenty of evidence supporting that belief. Zack Baun led Philadelphia with 12 tackles , finishing just four shy of crafting a new career high.

He was active against the run, effective in coverage, and involved in nearly every significant defensive sequence. Jihaad Campbell wasn't far behind with nine tackles while adding a sack, a tackle for loss, and another quarterback hit.

Combined, the duo accounted for 21 tackles and consistently helped clean up plays before they became bigger problems. If this becomes the weekly standard, or close to it, opposing offenses will have a hard time attacking the middle of Philadelphia's defense.

The Eagles were efficient in the red zone.

The Eagles didn't dominate offensively, but they capitalized when opportunities presented themselves. Philadelphia converted two of its three trips inside the red zone into touchdowns, a success rate any coaching staff will gladly accept. Dallas Goedert scored the first touchdown of the Eagles' season, while Dontayvion Wicks added another later in the game.

The offense remains a work in progress. Too many drives stalled, and too many possessions ended before they truly began.

Still, red-zone efficiency often separates wins from losses in tightly contested games. The Eagles weren't perfect Sunday, but they were productive enough where it mattered most.

Week 1 revealed plenty of areas that need improvement, but it also reinforced several truths Eagles fans have seen before. Hurts and Sirianni continue to start seasons well. Sirianni continues to thrive in close games. Philadelphia's linebackers appear poised for big years, and the offense showed it can finish drives when opportunities arise.

The Eagles may not have played their best football Sunday. The encouraging part is they still found a way to win anyway.

articles.title: NFC South Standings: Falcons bailed out by NFL's worst division
articles.summary: The Falcons weren't the only NFC South team to struggle in Week 1.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons struck out in their Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers , but luckily they play in the NFL's sorriest division and the other three NFC South teams also lost on Sunday. Collectively, the division went 0-4, but all four losses were of a different variety.

Starting with the Falcons, they played about as well as they could have on defense but their offense couldn't carry its weight despite a dominant performance by Bijan Robinson (173 all-purpose yards). The Steelers intercepted third-string quarterback Cooper Rush twice, including a pick-six, before sending Atlanta home with a 20-13 loss .

The New Orleans Saints trailed 21-0 to the Detroit Lions at Ford Field before going on an incredible second-half run and sending the game into overtime. The Lions scored first to go up 31-24, but the Saints answered with a touchdown of their own. However, they failed to convert a two-point conversion and the Lions held on for a 31-30 win.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had some Zac-Robinson-themed operation issues on offense in their 33-27 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on the road. Plus, Baker Mayfield lost three of four fumbles against the Bengals defense and the Bucs couldn't climb all the way back.

Last but not least, the Carolina Panthers lost a 59-37 shootout to the Chicago Bears at home. After getting off to slow start, the Panthers came back with a vengeance and made things interesting. Carolina ultimately couldn't stop Chicago's dynamic running game and still lost by 22 points to Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams .

The Falcons will host the Panthers in Week 2, while the Saints and Buccaneers will each face AFC North opponents. New Orleans will face Baltimore on the road, and Tampa Bay will host the Cleveland Browns .

NFL Week 1 isn't totally in the books just yet, though. The Kansas City Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos on Monday night to close out the opening week of the 2026 season.

articles.title: Malik Nabers says John Harbaugh tackled him to prove wideout could take a hit after knee surgery
articles.summary: John Harbaugh has a weird way of trying to prove a point.
articles.body:
New York Giants wideout Malik Nabers didn't put up star-caliber numbers Sunday night, but his performance was one of the most encouraging things to come out of the team's 28-20 win against the Dallas Cowboys .

In his first game back from knee surgery, Nabers hauled in six catches for 69 yards in the victory. In doing so, he proved he was back, healthy and was capable of taking hits after enduring a grueling rehab process.

That last aspect was something Nabers was worried about heading into the contest. Because of it, Nabers was a true game-time decision for Sunday's game. He didn't make the decision to play until roughly two hours before the game and did not invite his family to attend just in case he was not his usual self on the field, per ESPN.

In order to help Nabers be mentally prepared for his return, new Giants head coach John Harbaugh devised his own plan to ease Nabers' nerve. During team walkthrough, the head coach actually tried to tackle Nabers to prove the wideout was capable of taking hits.

Nabers said he did not go down on Harbaugh's tackle attempt.

Did that tactic work? Despite it, Nabers still needed until Sunday night before he was truly ready to take the field. Harbaugh's tackle attempt didn't fully convince the wideout to take the field, though it may have contributed. And if it didn't impact Nabers at all, at least he had a fantastic story to tell after the contest.

While Nabers' return was encouraging, the Giants still made sure to limit the wideout in his first game back since tearing his AC L last September. Nabers was on the field for 36 of the team's 68 offensive snaps.

His production and playing time should only increase as Nabers gains more confidence in his surgically-repaired knee.

That could come as early as Week 2, when the Giants are set to take on the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The extra day of recovery should help on that front as well.

Everything should be easier for Nabers now that he's finally cleared that mental hurdle. Because of that, we'd like to think Harbaugh will hold off on trying to tackle his star wideout again heading into Week 2.
